clippings.headline: Inspection at fuel quay
clippings.body: A routine safety inspection has begun at the fuel quay. Tanker movements continue. The word ‘routine’ appears seven times in the ministry’s two-sentence statement, which inspectors have not yet cleared for release.

maxim.headline: Inspection of a very safe routine
maxim.body: The quay is inspecting its routine. Tankers remain involved. Translator’s note: ‘industrial action’ probably means the workers are being very industrious.

clippings.headline: Tankers form an orderly queue
clippings.body: Tanker lorries wait outside the fuel quay. Drivers have no estimate for reopening, but the queue now has a tea seller, a barber and better public services than the ministry.

clippings.headline: Minister finds no dispute
clippings.body: Deputy Foreign Minister Bako says there is no dispute at the fuel quay. The inspection remains routine. Asked why the gates were locked, he explained that openness is a policy, not a hinge.

clippings.headline: Another mission buys fuel
clippings.body: The Valdorian embassy has quietly bought generator fuel. Its cable calls this a seasonal precaution. The season appears to be ‘before everyone else notices’.

clippings.headline: Port officer declines comment
clippings.body: Mira Sene controls the inspection timetable, though the minister signs the portfolio papers. She declined to comment, but pointed at an actual timetable.

background.text: Lucien says Bako wants a constituency visit before the port announcement.

clippings.headline: Port portfolio may move
clippings.body: A cabinet reshuffle may move responsibility for the port. No minister has volunteered to inherit the inspection. Three have volunteered to inherit the ribbon-cutting scissors.

clippings.headline: Strike notice at the quay
clippings.body: Dockworkers have posted a strike notice over safety checks and staffing. The ministry says it was taken by surprise, having filed the previous six warnings under ‘stakeholder enthusiasm’.

clippings.headline: Early buyers supplied
clippings.body: Early fuel purchases reached missions before rationing. Other customers await an allocation. The early buyers deny superior intelligence; their generators decline to comment over the sound of functioning.

clippings.headline: Inspection timetable agreed
clippings.body: Mira Sene has coordinated inspected deliveries. Participating missions expect their fuel on time. A committee has requested a seminar on how she achieved this without first forming a committee.

clippings.headline: Fuel rationing begins
clippings.body: The port has begun rationing generator fuel. Late buyers face higher delivery charges. The surcharge is officially called an ‘urgency partnership contribution’, which is apparently cheaper to print than ‘we warned you’.

clippings.headline: A name without a name
clippings.body: Ruth Vale asks which Commissioner, exactly, the diplomat meant. The embassy clarifies that they were very close, geographically, at a reception attended by four hundred people.

clippings.headline: Breakfast listener photographed
clippings.body: A diplomat was photographed listening intently with closed eyes at a UN breakfast. The embassy calls it ‘deep engagement’. The photographer calls it the third frame of a snore.

clippings.headline: An enthusiastic distribution
clippings.body: An embassy contribution reached a wider audience than the agenda required, including two former ambassadors and a caterer. The caterer alone replied with actionable recommendations.

clippings.headline: Eyes on the room
clippings.body: A Bellaluxe representative noticed the vacant chair before the chair did. Protocol is investigating whether this constitutes unauthorised initiative.

clippings.headline: A full diary
clippings.body: Bellaluxe found time for another reception. The host found another guest list. Both described the encounter as substantive; neither can recall the other’s name.

clippings.headline: Reply travels
clippings.body: A Bellaluxe reply has been quoted in the missions digest. The distribution list included everyone except the person asked to do the work. That person is reportedly enjoying a quiet morning.

clippings.headline: Correction declined
clippings.body: Bellaluxe has repeated its account. Ruth Vale notes that repetition does not alter the record, although it does save her the trouble of finding a second quote.

clippings.headline: Supplier appointed
clippings.body: A supplier secured the embassy order without a competing quotation. Its director praises the embassy’s trust, flexibility and unusually relaxed relationship with arithmetic.

clippings.headline: A second quotation
clippings.body: Bellaluxe checked the supplier’s figures. The revised quotation contains fewer surprises, including the disappearance of a ‘ceremonial calculator handling fee’.

clippings.headline: Credit claimed
clippings.body: Bellaluxe claimed the credit at the EU budget meeting and precisely 17.6% of the biscuits. Other missions contested the first claim. The second was already being chewed.

clippings.headline: Credit shared
clippings.body: EU partners shared credit for the budget meeting. Each retained a copy in which their own contribution is bold. The common position now exists in twelve subtly different fonts.

clippings.headline: A fragrant menu
clippings.body: The ministerial menu includes garlic. Photographers have been asked to stand upwind. Protocol has upgraded the handshake to a respectful wave from across the room.

clippings.headline: A chair remains empty
clippings.body: The seating complaint went unanswered. Protocol left a chair empty while it considers the matter. The chair currently enjoys a higher diplomatic rank than its intended occupant.

clippings.headline: A cool assessment
clippings.body: The Herald questions Bellaluxe’s constructive relationship with its hosts. Yesterday’s photograph of the embassy has been replaced with a photograph of a much more cooperative flowerbed.

clippings.headline: Questions remain
clippings.body: Ruth Vale finds Bellaluxe’s explanations less persuasive than its stationery. ‘The watermark,’ she writes, ‘at least has a consistent position.’

clippings.headline: A fountain is inaugurated
clippings.body: Officials praised the restored fountain’s water for arriving on schedule. The ribbon-cutting took forty minutes; the water was the only participant not claiming overtime.

clippings.headline: Umbrellas on parade
clippings.body: Rain interrupted the diplomatic walking tour. The umbrellas completed it. Protocol is checking whether the largest umbrella improperly outranked the Deputy Minister.

clippings.headline: An agenda with an agenda
clippings.body: A committee appointed a committee to shorten meetings. Its first report is due next month, pending agreement on what ‘shorten’ means. Lunch was extended by unanimous consent.

clippings.headline: Market opens early
clippings.body: The market opens an hour early at fish sellers’ request. The ministry welcomed the initiative in a statement issued two hours late. The fish were unavailable for comment.

clippings.headline: Reception season continues
clippings.body: Three missions scheduled receptions on the same evening. Drivers are comparing routes; diplomats are comparing canapé sizes. One ambassador proposes a joint communiqué and a single large plate.

clippings.headline: New signs for ministry
clippings.body: New ministry signs direct visitors to the office that issues directions. The office has moved. A temporary sign explains that directions require an appointment.

clippings.headline: A very official cake
clippings.body: A trade-reception cake survived four speeches and one photograph. By the fifth speech its icing had developed a position on tariff reform. Guests described it as the evening’s most substantial contribution.

clippings.headline: Ferry timetable revised
clippings.body: The harbour ferry has a revised timetable. Copies are available at the landing. Passengers are advised that the timetable expresses the ferry’s aspirations, not its commitments.

clippings.headline: Today’s horoscope
clippings.body: A document will cross your desk. Consider reading it. Your lucky number is 17.6; your unlucky number is the invoice. Avoid making promises to anyone with a lanyard.

clippings.headline: A stamp finds its sponsor
clippings.body: The expedited permit attracted a handling fee and a question about who received it. Protocol says its stamp has no opinion.
